primary_sources.source: Republic Act No. 12234, Konektadong Pinoy Act
primary_sources.relevance: Section 2 makes digital inclusivity and narrowing the digital divide national policy and calls for reliable and affordable universal internet access, expressly including disaster preparedness, public safety, e-governance, and basic services. The Act reforms the data-transmission market and assigns sector responsibilities; it does not guarantee connectivity to an individual application or locality.

Applies broadly to government offices including LGUs and directs a citizen-centered, secure, interoperable, inclusive transition to e-governance while balancing information access and privacy. It is relevant when a participating government office adopts the service, but it does not turn a private prototype into an official government platform or transfer public authority to the startup.

Provides testable, technology-neutral accessibility success criteria. Relevant Level A and AA requirements include text alternatives, keyboard access, reflow, contrast, error identification, labels and instructions, status messages, focus visibility/not obscured, target size, redundant entry, and accessible authentication. Conformance requires all applicable criteria for complete pages and processes, not selected checks alone.

primary_sources.source: 2024 National Information and Communications Technology Household Survey preliminary results
primary_sources.relevance: PSA reports that 48.8% of Philippine households had internet access at home in 2024. This establishes a material access gap at national level and supports testing low-bandwidth and non-digital contingencies; it does not measure availability during a specific disaster, Zamboanga City conditions, service quality, or access among the proposed users.

evidence.legal_or_evidentiary_status: RA 12234 and RA 12254 are binding Philippine statutes, but their duties attach to the actors and activities within their coverage; citing them is not evidence that the prototype complies or has resilient connectivity. WCAG 2.2 is an internationally recognized normative technical standard, not automatically a Philippine statutory obligation in every private deployment; the paper may adopt Level AA as an engineering and evaluation target. PSA NICTHS figures are empirical estimates subject to survey definitions and sampling. Draft preservation, idempotent retry, reconciliation, plain language, multilingual support, and alternative-channel procedures are defensible design inferences from the access and continuity problem, not provisions that these sources explicitly prescribe for this application.
evidence.evidence_limits_and_conflicts: The national 48.8% household-access statistic cannot be converted into a local outage rate, user-level exclusion rate, or proof that mobile data is unavailable. Household access also differs from an authorized reporter's workplace access, device ownership, digital literacy, affordability, latency, and disaster-time service. WCAG conformance cannot be inferred from automated scanners: keyboard, screen-reader, zoom/reflow, cognitive accessibility, error recovery, and complete task flows require human testing. WCAG does not cover every disability or guarantee usability. RA 12234 seeks better connectivity but infrastructure reform is not application availability. RA 12254 supports e-governance but does not authorize this startup to approve or submit official records. No source here establishes that English-only or Filipino-only content is adequate for all target jurisdictions. Demographic fields may help equity analysis yet increase re-identification risk, especially in small barangays or rare casualty categories; only necessary, authorized, proportionate fields and suitably aggregated outputs should be used.

chapter_one_integration.objective_revisions: Retain the six module objectives and add testable inclusion behavior within them rather than inventing a seventh module. User and Organization Management: accessible authentication that does not rely solely on cognitive tests, keyboard-complete account tasks, language preference where implemented, and recovery that does not expose another tenant. Disaster Reporting: responsive forms, explicit save state, local draft preservation where safe, attachment-size/type feedback, resumable or retryable submission, and protection against duplicate creation after interruption. Verification: accessible status and error messages, retained reviewer input, conflict warning when a record changed, and no silent overwrite. SitRep Generation: progress/failure state, retry without duplicate reports, provenance after reconciliation, and accessible generated output. Catalog: keyboard/search access, readable exports, and identification of superseded versions. Dashboard: text equivalents for charts, non-color status cues, table or record access to underlying values, reflow, and no auto-refresh that disrupts assistive technology. Evaluation: run complete role tasks on declared phone, tablet, and desktop viewports; keyboard-only and screen-reader checks; 200% and 400% zoom/reflow; low bandwidth, timeout, dropped request, refresh, duplicate retry, stale-version conflict, restoration, and approved paper/radio-to-system reconciliation scenarios.
chapter_one_integration.scope_inclusions: Include authorized reporters, reviewers, verifiers, approvers, viewers, customer administrators, startup support personnel, and users with visual, motor, auditory, cognitive, language, or age-related access needs. Connected browser access covers supported smartphones, tablets, and desktops. Connected degraded operation includes slow upload, latency, intermittent requests, timeouts, loss before or after server acknowledgement, expired sessions, and safe recovery. Preserve a draft only for the minimum necessary time and protect it from another user of a shared device; show whether data is saved locally, saved to server, submitting, submitted, failed, or requires reconciliation. Include an organization-approved continuity procedure using radio, telephone, paper, or face-to-face reporting when the web service cannot be used, followed by controlled later encoding that records original source, event time, receipt time, encoder, and duplicate/reconciliation outcome. Inclusion analysis should examine geographic coverage, role, device, connection, disability access needs, language, age group where lawful and relevant, and non-user exclusion without publishing identifiable small cells.
chapter_one_integration.limitations_and_delimitations: The prototype remains connected-web software: no offline synchronization, native app, SMS gateway, radio integration, satellite link, mesh network, custom hardware, or promise of operation without electricity or telecommunications. Browser-side draft preservation is not equivalent to offline workflow and may be disabled for sensitive data or shared devices. A retry mechanism cannot recover information never saved locally or received by the server. Accessibility evaluation supports only the declared WCAG 2.2 criteria, browsers, assistive technologies, languages, devices, tasks, and participants; it does not establish universal accessibility or formal certification. Translation is limited to languages actually implemented and professionally or community reviewed; machine or ad hoc translation of emergency terminology should not be claimed accurate. Survey participants and digitized reports may underrepresent disconnected, remote, low-literacy, disabled, older, or otherwise marginalized people. The system does not replace authorized contingency channels, field verification, public warning systems, emergency dispatch, or official communications.
chapter_one_integration.significance_causal_chains: Authorized reporter: responsive accessible form plus visible save/submission state -> a report can be completed and interruption recognized -> fewer avoidable abandoned or duplicate submissions may occur, provided the user has a compatible device, training, power, some connectivity, and an accessible workflow; harms include cached sensitive data and false confidence that an unacknowledged report arrived. Verifier/approver: retry-safe records, conflict warnings, and reconciliation lineage -> distinguish original observation, later encoding, duplicate, and correction -> more accountable review, provided procedures and staffing exist; harms include bottlenecks and mistaken merging. DRRM organization: tested degraded behavior plus approved non-digital contingency -> continue collecting observations during service loss and encode later -> reduce dependence on a single channel, provided radio/paper/telephone procedures, identifiers, custody, and drills exist; harms include delayed entry and conflicting copies. Persons with disabilities and language minorities: WCAG-aligned tasks, understandable labels, non-color cues, and reviewed language support -> greater possibility of independent task completion -> broader participation, provided representative users test real workflows; harms include token accessibility that passes automated checks but fails actual users. Community: broader input and cautious aggregation -> missing localities or groups may become visible -> follow-up can be prioritized, provided data is lawful and interpreted as reporting coverage rather than disaster incidence; harms include stigma and re-identification. Startup: measurable accessibility and continuity obligations -> clearer service acceptance and support requirements -> stronger adoption evidence, provided costs and residual risks are disclosed.
chapter_one_integration.safe_claims_and_claims_to_avoid: Safe: 'The prototype targets WCAG 2.2 Level AA for the implemented end-to-end tasks and will report criterion-, browser-, and assistive-technology-specific test results.' Safe: 'The system preserves submission state and supports controlled retry and reconciliation under tested intermittent-connectivity scenarios; organizations must retain approved non-digital procedures for complete outages.' Safe: 'PSA reported home internet access for 48.8% of households in 2024, supporting the need to avoid assuming universal connectivity.' Safe: 'RA 12234 identifies reliable and affordable universal internet access, including disaster preparedness and public safety, as national policy.' Avoid: 'The system is fully accessible,' 'works offline,' 'guarantees continuous disaster reporting,' 'complies with RA 12234/12254 because it is online,' 'eliminates the digital divide,' 'includes all communities,' or 'demographic dashboard differences prove inequitable disaster impact.' Avoid treating a saved browser draft as a successfully submitted official report or an automated WCAG score as conformance.

system_and_governance.authority_and_responsibility_matrix: Reporter creates observations, confirms submission acknowledgement, and uses the approved alternate channel when unavailable. Verifier determines evidentiary status and resolves suspected duplicates/conflicts; approver authorizes the SitRep version under organization procedure. Customer administrator assigns accessible roles and contingency contacts but cannot grant startup personnel verification authority. The participating organization owns continuity procedures, language choices, reasonable accommodations, official submission, records custody, lawful demographic collection, and reconciliation rules. Its privacy/records officers determine lawful basis, minimization, local-draft policy, retention, small-cell disclosure controls, and disposition. The startup implements accessible interaction, tenant isolation, state/acknowledgement display, retry safeguards, logs, backups, incident support, and tested export/recovery under contract. Connectivity providers operate transmission services under applicable law but are not guarantors of application correctness. External agencies determine whether and how they accept outputs. No retry, accessibility feature, or support role transfers incident verification or official approval to the startup.
system_and_governance.workflow_lineage_and_data_lifecycle: Use explicit client and server states: editing-unsaved, draft-local if permitted, draft-server, submitting with a client-generated request identifier, accepted with immutable server identifier and receipt timestamp, failed-known, outcome-unknown, returned, validated/rejected, reconciled/duplicate-linked, approved, corrected/superseded, archived/disposed. On timeout, query by request identifier before creating another record; repeated identical submissions must return the existing result or flag review. Preserve incident time separately from submission, server receipt, later encoding, verification, and approval times. Reconciliation records the alternate-channel source, original observer, receiver, encoder, time received, time encoded, matched records, selected authoritative version, reason, and responsible reviewer. Never silently merge conflicting casualty or affected-population figures. Encrypt and expire permitted local drafts, provide user-controlled deletion, avoid caches on shared devices where risk outweighs benefit, and disclose draft location. Apply retention and disposition to drafts, attachments, logs, exports, and superseded versions; accessibility labels and language must remain associated with records where needed for correct interpretation.
system_and_governance.module_specific_requirements: User and Organization Management: semantic HTML, labeled controls, logical focus, keyboard access, accessible session and authentication errors, tenant-safe recovery, and organization-configured language/help. Disaster Reporting: small-screen reflow, step/status text, explicit unknown values, input purpose and error association, draft indicator, attachment constraints before upload, request identifier, and outcome-unknown recovery. Verification: keyboard-operable compare view, programmatic status messages, source/version display, conflict protection, and recorded reconciliation decision. SitRep Generation: accessible generation controls and output, non-blocking progress, deterministic retry using the same generation request, and no publication until authorized approval. Catalog: accessible search/filter names, focus preservation, sortable table semantics, version/supersession labels, and usable export. Dashboard: every visual has a text/table alternative; meaning is not color-only; aggregation definitions and last-updated time are shown; small groups are suppressed or generalized under organization policy; no chart is used to infer unreported incidence.
system_and_governance.risk_controls_and_residual_limits: Connectivity controls: explicit acknowledgement, request IDs, bounded retries, exponential backoff, duplicate detection, stale-write protection, compact payloads, upload limits, and manual reconciliation. Accessibility controls: WCAG 2.2 AA acceptance criteria, semantic native controls, automated checks plus keyboard/screen-reader/zoom/user testing, accessible documents, and defect severity tied to task blockage. Inclusion controls: purposive recruitment across roles, devices, connection qualities, disability access needs, languages, and jurisdictions; record non-participation and alternate-channel reports. Privacy controls: minimize demographic granularity, separate identity from analysis, suppress/combine small cells, restrict exports, log access, and review combinations that re-identify individuals. Residual limits remain: total power/network loss, shared-device exposure, unsupported assistive technology, inaccessible third-party files, delayed reconciliation, human duplicate decisions, unreported events, sampling bias, and the possibility that aggregation still identifies a person in a small locality.

evaluation_and_feasibility.metrics_comparators_and_test_conditions: Report task completion as successful participants divided by participants attempting each complete role task, with errors and assistance separately. Accessibility: applicable WCAG 2.2 A/AA criteria passed divided by applicable criteria, plus blocker counts from keyboard-only, screen-reader, 200%/400% zoom, reflow, focus, labels/errors, target-size, and authentication tests; do not average away a critical blocked task. Connectivity: acknowledged submissions/attempts; duplicate records after retry/unique logical submissions; recovered drafts/interrupted drafts; correctly reconciled alternate-channel reports/reconciliation cases; data-field agreement before and after recovery; median and percentile completion time. Test at declared latency, bandwidth, packet/request interruption, timeout timing, payload sizes, devices, browsers, and roles, including loss before send, after server commit but before response, during upload, refresh, login expiry, and concurrent edit. Compare against the current paper/informal-message procedure for the same scripted dataset where feasible, not against an assumed perfect baseline. Inclusion: describe participant counts and completion by relevant group only where sample size and privacy permit; otherwise provide qualitative barriers without inferential claims.
evaluation_and_feasibility.adoption_cost_and_service_dependencies: Adoption requires compatible devices and browsers, connectivity/data costs, power, accessible training and support, language review, customer administrators, contingency-channel equipment and forms, drills, reconciliation staffing, hosting, monitoring, backups, security updates, accessibility regression testing, incident response, and export/provider-exit capability. Procurement or subscription pricing must include support, storage/attachments, recovery objectives, accessibility remediation, migration, connectivity, training, and transition—not only license price. Service levels should distinguish application uptime from end-to-end user connectivity and state maintenance/incident windows, support channels, recovery targets, acknowledgement semantics, and customer duties. Broader adoption needs evidence that target organizations can staff verification and reconciliation and that excluded users retain an effective alternate route.
evaluation_and_feasibility.generalization_and_future_evidence: Current evidence supports a bounded responsive-web prototype evaluated in named organizations, roles, hazards, devices, browsers, assistive technologies, languages, network profiles, and scenarios. It does not generalize to all Philippine LGUs, islands, disabilities, indigenous or local languages, large disasters, nationwide concurrency, prolonged outages, or populations absent from digital records. Production claims require multi-site and seasonal pilots; representative disabled-user and low-literacy testing; local connectivity measurements including disaster periods; translation/terminology validation; high-volume and long-outage reconciliation drills; independent accessibility and security assessment; recovery exercises; small-cell and linkage re-identification testing; alternate-channel effectiveness measures; and longitudinal evidence of adoption, support load, cost, data quality, and dropout. Outcome claims such as faster response or more equitable assistance additionally require a prospective comparator, operational confounder measurement, and ethically governed outcome data.
